_doc: THE UTILITY LAYER — an orthogonal axis, not a primitive. MEASURED: after `subtitle`, the most-shared vocabulary in the 73-doc corpus is bare tone modifiers applied to arbitrary elements (green 27 docs, amber 25, purple 23, red 20, tight 12). No primitive can absorb that, because a tone is not a thing — it is a property of any thing. Every rule here binds to a palette token, never a literal colour, so `--style` swaps the whole look without touching the markup (Covenant II: colour means things, and it must keep meaning them in every style). Emission is USAGE-SCANNED: a page that uses none of these classes receives zero bytes of this CSS, which is what keeps every existing golden byte-identical. Authors never supply a raw class — templates map an author TOKEN through a lookup table (the `code` primitive's pattern), so this vocabulary is whitelisted by construction and is not an injection surface. See docs/design/leaf-gap-worklist.md §4 Tier 3.
